priceSnapshot.note: THIS IS A LATE MIDNIGHT RUN AND THE MARKET DID NOT WAIT. The session fired at 08:33 COT rather than 02:00, and yesterday's endday session never produced a file, so the comparison base is the 20 August MIDDAY report at 72,738.7 - twenty hours of tape rather than the usual nine. In that window BTC ran from a 72,328.0 low to a 79,515.7 high, a 9.94 percent excursion, and has since given back 2,683.8 points of it. The 04:00Z 4H bar closed 76,305.9 and the 08:00Z bar printed the 79,515.7 high and then closed 76,730.1 - a 2,785.6-point upper wick on a single four-hour candle, which is the signature of a spike that ran out of buyers rather than a breakout that is being built on. Both of midday's gates fired again and in the same punishing order: the reduce line at 72,508.0 broke first on an 18:00Z hourly close of 72,431.9, 76.1 points through, and the add gate at 73,185.0 then cleared on the 00:00Z close of 73,714.3. sessionRange below is measured from the 20 August 17:45Z 15m bar - the first bar after the midday snapshot - to now.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $75,750.0 - underneath the 9,491,076 USD of freshly liquidated longs stacked at 76,500 and 76,250. Spot sits 1,081.9 points above it and the 1H ATR is 1,011.8, so this is very slightly more than one ordinary hourly bar of room, which is deliberate: anything tighter is noise on a day with a 2,124.7 daily ATR. A settled close below it says the rejection off 79,515.7 was distribution rather than a shakeout, and the next shelf down is 75,000 and then the impulse base at 74,518.1.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $77,750.0 - the heaviest band in the whole twenty-four-hour liquidation tape at 10,104,413 USD, and the level the 12:30Z and 12:45Z 15m bars failed at when they topped out at 77,480.4. Reclaiming it on a close would mean the spike zone is being rebuilt rather than sold. Be honest about the cost of a break up here: 8,612,836 USD of the weight at 77,750 was SHORT liquidations that have already been paid out, so there is no trapped short book left to squeeze between 77,750 and 79,515.7. Any move through has to be funded with real spot demand.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from midday's ADD to TAKE_PROFIT, and it is a trim into strength rather than a change of trend view. Midday was right and is being paid: it deployed 18.00 USDT into the spot core at 72,738.7 on the fired add gate, and spot is 4,093.2 points higher. What has changed is that the reward has arrived and the risk has gone vertical. The 4H RSI is 91.5 and the daily is 84.4 - the most stretched readings anywhere in this file. Price is 15.8 percent above the daily EMA20 at 66,342.9 and 7.3 percent above the daily EMA200 at 71,604.1. The 08:00Z 4H bar left a 2,785.6-point upper wick. Two of midday's three constructive arguments have now inverted: open interest has turned UP hard, +5.42 percent to 2,325,363,464 USD against the 2,205,746,722 midday reading, so the new money is finally arriving - but it is arriving AFTER a 20 percent three-day move rather than before it; and funding has normalised from the 0.0000501 discount midday celebrated back to the full 0.0001 base with a 0.000204 premium, meaning the perpetual now trades ABOVE spot and longs are paying to hold. The long/short account ratio spiked to 1.33 at the 08:00Z print - the highest reading in this file - before settling to 1.10. The one thing that genuinely improved is flow: the 20 August Farside row that midday flagged as unresolved printed +606.3m, the largest single day in the visible window. That is why this is a partial trim of a winner and not an exit.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull reads DOWN, and for once the reason is not an artefact of where price has traded. The tape covers a full twenty-four hours including both the run to 79,515.7 and the rejection, so both sides of spot are genuinely measured. Of 96,386,076 USD of realized liquidations, 61,294,673 were shorts and 35,091,403 were longs - a 1.75 to 1 short-side flush, which is what drove the move. The forward-looking part is the composition by level, not the total. Every heavy band ABOVE spot is a spent short flush: 8,612,836 of the 10,104,413 at 77,750, and 3,004,132 of the 3,004,386 at 79,250. Those shorts are gone and cannot be squeezed again. The bands immediately BELOW spot are the opposite - 5,524,108 of the 6,438,313 at 76,500 and 2,495,894 of the 3,052,763 at 76,250 are LONG liquidations, freshly carved by the rejection, which is where stops are being rebuilt right now. Nearest above is 77,000 at 168.1 points and it too is long-dominated at 3,240,523. Add the long/short account ratio at 1.10 after touching 1.33 on the spike, and the crowded side is unambiguously the long side. That does not make the trend bearish; it makes the next 1,000 points cheaper to travel downward than upward.

atr.source: Wilder ATR(14) computed this run from a 600-bar OKX BTC-USDT 1Dutc candle window ending on the live 21 August bar. pct is against the current 76,831.9. Shorter horizons from the same live series: 1,348.6 on the 4H, 1,011.8 on the 1H and 575.2 on the 15m. Every one of those has expanded since the midday report - the daily from 1,753.3, the 4H from 1,014.3, the 1H from 669.7 and the 15m from 355.8, which is a 61.7 percent expansion on the fifteen-minute series alone. Volatility is now expanding on EVERY horizon simultaneously, including the one that had stalled. That is the opposite of the reading midday took and it is the single strongest argument for taking money off the table rather than adding to it.

etfFlows.note: The question midday left open has been answered, and it was answered with the biggest number in the visible window. The 20 August Farside row printed +606.3m, extending the streak to four consecutive inflow days: 17 August +297.5m, 18 August +189.3m, 19 August +517.2m and 20 August +606.3m, for +1,610.3m in total. Midday wrote that if the 20 August row came in positive, the reclaim of 72,508.0 had a funding source; it did, and the market has since added another 5.6 percent on top. This is the single strongest bullish datum in the report and it is why the trend read stays bullish while the tilt turns down. The 21 August row is still 0.0 because US funds have not reported today.

liquidations.note: skew is the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio at the 13:00Z print, not a USD ratio. Its path over the spike is the story: 1.10 at 04:00Z, 1.04 at 06:00Z, 1.11 at 07:00Z, then 1.33 at 08:00Z as price ran to 79,515.7 - the highest account ratio anywhere in this file - before unwinding through 1.17, 1.16, 1.05 and back to 1.10 now. Longs piled in AT the high and were promptly liquidated; the 6,438,313 USD of mostly-long fills at 76,500 and 3,052,763 at 76,250 are those accounts. Open interest tells the matching story from the other side: 2,325,363,464 USD, up 5.42 percent from midday's 2,205,746,722, so this leg finally has NEW positioning behind it rather than short covering - which is exactly what midday said was missing. The catch is timing. New leverage arriving after a 20 percent three-day move is late leverage, and funding confirms it: the rate is back at the full 0.0001 base with a 0.000204 premium, so the perpetual trades above spot and longs are paying to hold, against the 0.0000501 discount midday recorded. longsUsd and shortsUsd are the realized twenty-four-hour totals across 7,134 fills.

calibration.rollingRecord: Midday published reduce 72,508.0 and add 73,185.0. Both fired, reduce first: the 18:00Z hourly bar closed 72,431.9, exactly 76.1 points through the reduce line, before the 00:00Z bar closed 73,714.3 and cleared the add gate by 529.3 points. This is the second consecutive session in which BOTH of the prior report's gates fired and the downside one fired first on a shallow break.
calibration.note: The whipsaw is now a pattern rather than an accident and it deserves a name: this file keeps setting reduce lines inside one hourly ATR of spot, and price keeps clipping them by under a hundred points before going the other way. Midday's reduce line sat 230.7 points under spot against a 669.7 1H ATR - roughly one third of a normal bar - and it broke by 76.1 points on a close and then never traded there again. Anyone who acted on the published reduce sold at 72,431.9 and watched 4,400 points of upside. What SAVED the session is that midday did not act on its own reduce line; it acted on the add, deploying 18.00 USDT at 72,738.7, and that decision is up 5.63 percent. So actingHelped is true for the trade actually taken and would have been false for the gate published. Today's reduce line at 75,750.0 is set 1,081.9 points away, slightly more than one 1H ATR of 1,011.8, specifically to stop repeating this.
